reason: B is more specific and testable: it defines a 5–10 nm FCC regime, an SRO-inducing treatment, measurable premelting and melting shifts, and heating above the expected melting point, whereas A’s 1000–1200 K ceiling may never measure melting. Its main weakness is that annealing versus quenching can also alter defects, segregation, and morphology, so these confounders must be controlled to isolate SRO.
